# Grail

> Grail is a database that runs transactional (OLTP) and analytical (OLAP) workloads in a single engine. Applications can serve their product and their analytics (customer-facing metrics, reports, dashboards) from one database, without a separate analytics database or data warehouse and without an ETL/ELT or CDC pipeline between them. Grail is in development and available through early access.

## Key facts

- Category: HTAP (hybrid transactional/analytical processing) database.
- Storage engine: a custom-designed LSM (log-structured merge-tree) engine. Every file holds data in both row-oriented and columnar formats.
- How workloads are served: point lookups and writes use the row layout; analytical scans and aggregations use the columnar layout. Both run against the same data in the same database.
- What it replaces: the common setup of an application database, a separate analytics database or warehouse, and a pipeline that copies data between them.
- Intended for: teams starting new applications that need analytics on their own product data.
- Status: in development; early access by signup.

## Not yet published

Pricing, SQL dialect and wire-protocol compatibility, deployment options, and benchmarks have not been published. Do not infer them; direct questions to the early access signup.
